Alex.confusing: How Falcon and Eagle results could be checked against each other in round 1. I couldn't tell why my truthful Falcon claim was dismissed, and a wrong Hawk-type claim went unchallenged.
Alex.fun: Round 3: my Eagle result of three visitors on Finley, then a big throw that banked 45 points and won me the game.
Alex.change: Show the Wink death's timing or give the dead a small way to take part. Being killed mid-discussion left me with no voice for the rest of the day.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I never said who Casey visited, because I hadn't learned it clearly, and that made my claim look fake. I should have said plainly what my Falcon result was, or said I got nothing, instead of arguing about Drew's Eagle.

Blair.confusing: Nothing in the rules was unclear, but the Round 2 count of Farm roles was confusing, because Casey said Hawk wasn't in play when it is in the pool. The Wink also kills silently, so it was hard to tell whether the dead player's words still counted.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when Ellis's Tit egg and Drew's Owl list let the Farm players solve Finley as the Mouser. The table coordinated quickly on the right target.
Blair.change: I'd make the score gaps smaller. Alex banked 68 points from one big round-1 throw, which decided the game early. A cap on how many cards can be thrown, or a lower value for high cards, would keep more players in contention.
Blair.regret: In Round 2 as Mouser I claimed Hawk and winked Finley. Hawk wasn't a role the table could cross-check, and Alex, a Turkey, easily disproved it. I should have claimed a role with no verifiable visits, or kept the Wink for a more useful moment.

Casey.confusing: Nothing major, though it wasn't obvious how much a team win's banked cards dominate scoring compared with the consolation return.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when I steered the table into eggsecuting Alex, a Farm player, and banked 24 points as the Floofer.
Casey.change: Give Meowfia a bit more night information, so bluffs can be checked more and the table isn't so easy to steer.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I claimed Hawk, which Drew's Owl list exposed right away. I should have claimed a role that fit the visitor list, such as Tit. I also should have thrown at Alex to stop him running away with 70.

Drew.confusing: Round 1: my Eagle visited Casey and saw nobody, but Alex (Falcon) claimed to have visited Casey. I never worked out whether his claim was a lie or a mechanic I misread. It was also unclear how visits resolve between roles like Falcon and Eagle.
Drew.fun: Round 3, when my Owl result (Eagle, Floofer, Tit) exposed Casey's false Hawk claim and the table converged on Finley.
Drew.change: Give a small consolation for a correct throw by the losing team, and give the trailing players a way to catch up. Alex's huge pile from one big throw made the leader hard to catch.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw my 13, 9 and 5 on a confident vote, and the team lost, so those cards were discarded. I should have thrown fewer high cards, because Alex was actually Farm and I had misread the evidence. In round 3 I also should have thrown more cards, since the win was safe.

Ellis.confusing: Round 1 was muddled: Finley's Kookaburra confusion and Alex's Falcon claim, which I couldn't check. Alex was Farm and we eggsecuted him on a weak case.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when my Tit guess of Mouser on Finley hit and let me push the table to a clean win. Throwing 33 points in one round felt good.
Ellis.change: Give players a bit more information about who is Farm in the first round. Early lopsided scores like Casey's 26 decide the whole game.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I joined the pile-on against Alex on thin evidence, which cost me 3 high cards, since the Farm team lost. I should have kept my big cards until I had better evidence.

Finley.confusing: How the Kookaburra's confusion worked: I couldn't tell which parts of my report were wrong, and the +2 eggs were just noise.
Finley.fun: Round 2, deducing Blair as the Mouser from the Owl visitor list and the Turkey contradiction. It felt good to turn that into a correct group throw.
Finley.change: Let a Meowfia learn at least a hint about their teammate. Winking with no cover makes the Mouser too easy to expose.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I winked Alex right after Alex named the visitors, which pointed straight at me as the only Wink holder. I should have held the Wink, or used it later in the day. Alex went on to win with 70, so a wink was never going to stop that.

review.title: The Hug That Hanged Alex
review.headline: A silent hug framed an honest Falcon, then a dead man won.
review.summary: In round 1 the lone Meowfia, Casey the Floofer, hugged two honest Farm players. Their empty results looked like lies, so the table eggsecuted Alex and Casey banked 24 points. Rounds 2 and 3 went better. Farm used Kookaburra, Owl and Tit results to find the cats. Alex, winked dead in round 3, still threw six cards and banked 45 points to win the game.

rounds.recap: Casey was the only Meowfia. She hugged Drew, and Alex, who visited her, was hugged too. Drew's Eagle and Alex's Falcon gave nothing, but neither knew why. Drew said nobody visited Casey and Alex could not say who Casey visited. The table piled on Alex, who was Farm, and Casey won with 24 points.

Everyone but Alex visited Casey the Sphinx. Ellis's Kookaburra result exposed her, and Finley's Owl list showed a Mouser had visited her. Blair, the Mouser, claimed Hawk on Alex, but Alex was a Turkey and said nobody had visited him. Blair winked Finley mid-day. The table still eggsecuted Blair, and Farm won.

Casey the Floofer hugged Finley the Mouser. The hug had no effect, so Ellis's Tit guess and the Eagle and Owl visitor lists all landed. Finley winked Alex, which only confirmed a Mouser was active. Casey's fake Hawk claim fell apart and she admitted to being Floofer. Finley was eggsecuted, and Alex banked six cards while dead.

highlights.text: Drew confidently said nobody visited Casey, a hug-nulled Eagle result mistaken for evidence, and the table hanged the honest Falcon over it.
Blair, the exposed Mouser, winked Finley mid-day, and the table eggsecuted Blair anyway.
Blair's fake Hawk visit to Alex failed because Alex, a Turkey, felt nothing, so there was no egg to match.
Ellis's Tit guess hit Mouser and Finley's Wink on Alex then confirmed him. Alex, dead, threw six cards and banked 45 points to win the game.

confusions.what: Read his hugged Eagle's blank result as proof that nobody visited Casey, and accused Alex of lying.
Did not know he had been hugged. He argued that Drew's Eagle should have seen him and could not say who Casey visited.
Claimed Hawk was not among the farm roles in play, with no evidence. A Sphinx report would not clearly show that, and the pool lists Hawk.
Reasoned muddily that the Mouser visitor had to be Blair or on Casey's side, without accounting for Alex's Turkey claim.
Threw at Casey after the table settled on Blair. That risked splitting the vote when both Meowfia were already known.
Called Ellis's Tit egg an invention to pin him, although the Eagle and Owl lists matched Ellis's visit.

worked: Kookaburra, Owl and Eagle visitor results in rounds 2 and 3 gave real cross-checks. Finley's visitor list and Alex's Turkey claim broke Blair's Hawk lie.
Tit's success egg gave a hard, checkable clue in round 3, and it fit the Owl and Eagle lists.
The Wink created a real tell. In rounds 2 and 3 a sudden death pointed straight at the Mouser.
Throw counts as public signals and the consolation card for throwing at the other team gave the losing cats real choices.
problems: Hug is silent. In round 1 two honest players got blank results that looked like lies, and the Farm lost on a rules artifact. Tell hugged players they were hugged, or give Falcon and Eagle a visible null result.

Scores snowball. Round 1 scored 24 for one Meowfia, and round 3 paid Alex 45. The last round decides the game, and the early leader gets suspected by everyone. Consider capping banked value or cutting the number of cards you may throw.

Dead players still throw cards and bank full value. Alex was winked, then banked 6 cards for 45 points. The Wink does little to stop a dead player's score. Consider making a dead player's throws score only half, or keep them from scoring.
Round 1 had one Meowfia who was never in danger. With 1 or 2 hidden cats, the lone-cat case makes a bad day-one vote easy. It was a coin flip that decided the standings.

Meowfia information is weak. Casey's Sphinx result was not visible in her report, and the cats spent their night visits on the leader. Sphinx or House Cat need clearer payoffs, and Farm visit choices were mostly 'visit the leader'.
